label: models/fw_drum.mdl: a rusted 55-gallon drum with a hazard stripe

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_longjump.mdl, models/rip.mdl, models/uplant1.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked B, C, B, A where the asset was D, A, C, C: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: The outline is a closed cylinder with a lid, a top chime, a bottom chime and a flat base in all ten views (sides.png). Nothing sticks out or is missing, and the shape fits a 55-gallon drum as the brief describes it.

M2.reason: Measured 24 x 24 x 36 against the brief's 23 across and 34 high: 4% and 6% off, within the 15% band. The measure reads 0.059 off.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies: body, lid, top chime ring, bottom chime ring, base, and the hazard band. All are present in the front and side views (the rings at about 70 and 308 px, the stripe at mid-height). The round body is faceted at about 12 sides in the top and bottom views; the brief sets no side count, so this is not charged. No bung is modelled; the brief does not ask for one.

M4.reason: The body is a uniform blue-grey painted steel with only faint mottling. The brief asks for a rusted drum, and no rust colour (orange or brown patches, flaking at the seams) shows on the body, lid or rings. The hazard yellow and black are correct.

M5.reason: The hazard stripe is sharp and in its place. The rust and wear the brief asks for are not there: no pitting, scrapes or rust streaks on the body, the chimes or the lid, only soft mottling. A rusted drum reads as a clean painted one.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up test. In the four readings of lineup.png the judges did not pick the asset (at D, A, C and C, they picked B, C, B and A), so it passed for one of the game's.

M7.reason: Stands upright on its flat base in every view, with the lid at the top. The brief sets no front, and the stripe sits at mid-height on the body.

M8.reason: SMAK's check is clean (no errors). Triangles are 240, under the 422 that Half-Life's most-built props of this kind and size spend, so it passes. It is over the third quartile (156), which is a warning, not a fail. The top, bottom and sides are closed in every view.
